bifrost: bifrost_app::keychain (springboard/sdk/src/keychain.rs), springboard/src/keychain.rs, springboard/proto/src/lib.rs (KeychainOp), springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs, springboard/src/shell/update.rs, springboard/src/shell/sha256.rs, springboard/sdk/src/url.rs, springboard/src/privd/auth.rs, springboard/src/shell/passcode.rs
summary: BifrOSt covers generic-password keychain items for apps (asynchronous, per-app store), app sandboxing, login authentication and HTTPS transport for the shell. It has no SDK API for code signing, certificate trust evaluation, Authorization Services, or the SecRandom and crypto transform calls, and it has no code signing or notarization at all. Refreshed 2026-10-17: Key objects and crypto transforms are covered by springboard/sdk/src/crypto_kit.rs (AesGcmKey, KeyAgreementKey, SigningKey, seal, open, sign, verify_signature; tests crypto_kit::tests), so that gap is closed.

features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/keychain.rs (add, get, update, delete); springboard/sdk/src/keychain_query.rs (ItemClass, Attributes, Query, MatchLimit, Status, add_item, copy_matching, update_items, delete_items); springboard/src/keychain.rs; springboard/proto/src/lib.rs (KeychainOp, KeychainStatus); wired: springboard/src/keychain.rs (Store::list, per-item modified time); springboard/sdk/src/passwords.rs; Settings > Passwords in springboard/src/shell/passwords_page.rs
features.note: Generic and internet passwords with attributes (label, comment, dates, access group) via the SDK query API; the shell store still keys by (service, account) and holds attributes inside the value. kSecMatchLimitAll needs a shell list operation (SDK filters with select). Errors mirror OSStatus codes. No certificate, key or identity classes, no access groups, no iCloud sync. Calls are asynchronous, unlike Apple's synchronous calls (docs/bifrost-ui.md, Keychain section). Wired into the UI in wiring wave 6 (0.5.44); verify on Midget for parity. Headless tests: sdk/tests/parity_sdk-tests-01a.rs (generic_password_wire_key_is_service_and_account, internet_password_wire_key_carries_server_port_and_protocol, an_item_round_trips_through_its_stored_record, a_legacy_value_decodes_as_a_generic_password_with_only_its_secret, a_damaged_record_is_a_decode_status, decode_item_maps_a_failed_get_to_its_status, a_query_matches_only_the_attributes_it_sets_and_the_same_class, match_limit_one_takes_the_first_hit_and_all_takes_every_hit, select_drops_the_secret_and_the_attributes_the_query_did_not_ask_for).

features.apple: Keychain data protection classes and Secure Enclave-backed keys
features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/keychain_protection.rs (Protection, DeviceState, readable, code, from_code); springboard/src/keychain.rs (BKC1 file, ChaCha20 plus HMAC-SHA256, per-app subkeys)
features.note: The six data protection classes, their wire codes and their readability rules are an SDK model with tests. The store still encrypts every item the same way, so the class is not enforced at rest, and there is no TPM or login-password key source.

features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/system/app_sandbox.rs (granted, permits, Capability); springboard/src/bare/app_policy.rs (Policy::from_permissions, with_entitlements, command)
features.note: Apps can read which capabilities their manifest grants, in manifest order, with tests. The bubblewrap sandbox is still built by the shell, with a separate app account and cgroups, and apps cannot change it or inspect its mounts. Apple's entitlement model is not used.

verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 24 tests. Wave 2 (theme-01, parity/integration e52c2fd0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. The privileged helper (privd) checks login through PAM for the shell. Apps have no authorization API, and the manifest permission is the only grant. docs/bifrost-ui.md records that the shell still runs as root (stage 2 is pending).

features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/local_auth.rs (LAContext, LAPolicy, LAError, decode_reply); springboard/sdk/src/system/authorization_lock.rs (PasswordError); springboard/src/privd/auth.rs; springboard/src/shell/passcode.rs (salted, stretched SHA-256 passcode with lockout)
features.note: The SDK models the authentication context, its policies and errors, and the reply of the account password check, with tests. The shell draws the prompt, the password check runs in the privileged daemon, and there is no biometry.
verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 13 tests. Apps get HTTPS through the shell's rustls stack. No SDK API to set or inspect the trust policy, pin certificates or read the peer certificate.

verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 10 tests. Wave 3 (theme-10, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. The Wi-Fi 802.1X sheet has a Don't Validate Server option, but that is a user choice in the network sheet, not a certificate API (springboard/src/shell/wifi_page.rs:56, NOTICE). The SDK has no certificate types.

Scheme and TLS choice, port defaults and redirect resolution are tested headless in url::transport_security_tests. The URL client refuses an https request redirected to plain http, and transport_policy decides plain-http exceptions per host and subdomain, tested headless in sdk/tests/parity_sdk-complete-35.rs. Gap: the URL client does not read an exception list from the app manifest yet, so exceptions apply only where an app calls TransportPolicy itself. The shell's update client (src/shell/update.rs) is HTTPS only.

features.apple: Code signing checks during Mac software updates (Updating Mac Software)
features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/system/update_integrity.rs (verify, Expected, IntegrityError); springboard/src/shell/update.rs (manifest sha256, size check); springboard/src/shell/sha256.rs
features.note: Apps can check a download against its announced size and SHA-256 digest with tests, as the shell does. The manifest is still not signed, so an attacker who controls the manifest controls the digest, and the check is only as trustworthy as the HTTPS source.

verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 6 tests. Wave 5 (w5-security, parity/integration 93f283b0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No code signing or signature verification found in the repo. Apps are installed without a signature check (store apps run from /var/lib/springboard/apps/<id>).

features.apple: Notarizing macOS software before distribution; Hardened Runtime
features.note: Apple's notary service has no BifrOSt counterpart. The Linux sandbox in app_policy.rs covers the same goal, but it is not a Hardened Runtime.

verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 6 tests. Wave 4 (w4-security, parity/integration 0925691e): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No SDK call returns random bytes to apps. Internal use only. Built 2026-10-17 (correction): the SDK entropy module is public to apps (copy_bytes, bytes, below); tests entropy::tests.

verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 9 tests. Wave 4 (w4-security, parity/integration 0925691e): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No SDK API for encryption, signing or key objects. Hashing and MAC are internal to the shell.

features.note: Depends on Apple's iCloud Keychain and associated domains. No BifrOSt counterpart.

verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 7 tests. Wave 3 (theme-28, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No SDK text-field content type for one-time codes or autofill from messages. features.apple: OSStatus values such as errSecDuplicateItem and errSecItemNotFound
features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/security_status.rs (KNOWN_CODES, category, meaning); springboard/sdk/src/keychain.rs (Error); Error::code() in docs/bifrost-ui.md
features.note: A table of the result codes the keychain and trust services return, each with a meaning and a category, is tested headless in sdk/tests/parity_sdk-complete-35.rs, and the keychain error codes are checked against it. Gap: the table covers only the codes this platform reports, and certificate, key and trust evaluation services have no counterpart yet. Headless tests: sdk/tests/parity_sdk-tests-01a.rs (osstatus_codes_match_the_security_framework_values).

features.feature: Legacy Secure Transport, Secure Download, CSSM
features.apple: Secure Transport, Secure Download, Common Security Services Manager
features.note: Deprecated Apple interfaces. No BifrOSt counterpart is needed.

gaps: Trust evaluation is a model over Ed25519-signed links (springboard/sdk/src/trust.rs; shell springboard/src/shell/services/trust_eval.rs); there is no DER certificate parsing and no SecIdentity or client-certificate type.

Update manifests are not signed: springboard/ui/src/ed25519.rs verifies signatures, but the shell update path (springboard/src/shell/update.rs) checks only a digest and size, and apps are not code-signed.
Authorization Services: an app-facing authorization API for privileged operations
Keychain item classes beyond generic and internet passwords (no certificate or key classes); the data protection classes are not enforced at rest (feature 1)
Keychain master key is on the same disk as the items (no TPM or login-password key source)
Synchronous keychain calls (Apple's are synchronous; BifrOSt's are asynchronous by design)
